answer: The tag is `#meta/template/slash`. A page with that tag defines a slash command, and the last component of the page name becomes the command's name (source: Slash Templates.md).

Memory for: Which tag turns a page into a slash template?
[1] Slash Templates.md (Creating a slash template)
  - Slash templates are defined as pages tagged with `#meta/template/slash`.
  Slash templates are a quick way to define [[Slash Command|slash commands]] that insert templated content at the cursor position. They are defined as pages tagged with `#meta/template/slash`. The inserted text is saved in the destination page. Later edits to the template do not change earlier insertions.
  - The advanced frontmatter key `onlyContexts` shows the slash command only in certain AST node contexts.
[2] Template.md (Creating templates)
  - Slash templates are pages tagged with `#meta/template/slash`, and they define slash commands that insert templated content at the cursor position.
  Slash templates: [[Slash Templates]] are pages tagged with `#meta/template/slash`. They define [[Slash Command|slash commands]] that insert templated content at the cursor position. The last component of the page name becomes the slash command name. / See also: [[API/template]], [[Page Template]], [[Slash Templates]], [[Space Lua]]
  A template in SilverBullet is a string that contains `${expression}` placeholders, which get evaluated using [[Space Lua]]. When a template runs, its placeholders are evaluated. Page and slash templates insert the resulting text into a page. That text stays saved until you edit it. A template called from a page expression renders a live result instead. See [[Guide/When Results Update]] for update behavior. / They are often used in [[Slash Templates]] and [[Page Template]].
[3] Slash Command.md (Built-in slash commands)
  - Most slash commands are implemented as Slash Templates, which are pages tagged #meta/template/slash whose content is inserted at the cursor.
  Slash templates: Most slash commands are implemented as [[Slash Templates]] — pages tagged with `#meta/template/slash` whose content is inserted at the cursor. The standard library includes slash templates for: / * `/query` — insert a SLIQ query block / * `/lua-query` — insert a Lua query expression / * `/code` — insert a fenced code block / * `/data` — insert a [[Tag/data|data block]], with the cursor where its tag goes / * `/table` — insert a Markdown table / * `/hr` — insert a horizontal rule / * `/note-admonition`, `/warning-admonition`, `/success-admonition`, `/danger-admonition` — insert admonition blocks / * `/tpl` — insert a template expression / * `/func` — insert a Lua function definition / * `/lua-command` — insert a command definition / * `/lua-slash-command` — insert a slash command definition
  - The /data slash template inserts a data block with the cursor where its tag goes.
  Defining your own: There are two ways to create custom slash commands: / 1. **Slash templates** (recommended): Create a page tagged `#meta/template/slash`. See [[Slash Templates]] for details. / 2. **`slashCommand.define`**: For slash commands that need logic beyond simple text insertion. See [[API/slashCommand#slashCommand.define(spec)]].
Exact facts:
- [1] 1. Run the `Page: From Template` command
- [1] 2. Select “Slash Template”
- [1] 3. Pick a name, the last component of the page name (after the `/` if any) will be used as the slash command’s name. For example, a page named `Library/Slash Template/action-items` creates a `/action-items` slash command.
- [1] 4. Put the template content in the page body. Lua directives (`${...}`) are supported and will be evaluated when the template is inserted.
- [1] Run the `System: Reload` command to activate the slash template.
